content: Certainly. 1. A pilot study was conducted and published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2010 (Volume 91, Issue 4, Pages 596-601). 2. Mountain AD, Kirby RL, Smith C, Eskes G, and Thompson K conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of powered wheelchair skills training for individuals who had experienced a stroke. The findings were published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2014 (Volume 93, Issue 12, Pages 1031-1043). 3. Mountain AD, Smith C, and Kirby RL explored the relevance of wheelchair skills assessment and training for long-term wheelchair users through two case reports. This study was published in Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology in 2010 (Volume 5, Issue 3, Pages 230-233). 4. Nisbet PD assessed and trained children for powered mobility in the United Kingdom. The results were published in Technology and Disability in 2002 (Volume 14, Issue 4, Pages 173-182). 5. Ozturk A and Ucsular FD evaluated the effectiveness of a wheelchair skills training program for community-dwelling manual wheelchair users in Turkey through a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in Clinical Rehabilitation in 2011 (Volume 25, Issue 5, Pages 416-424). 6. Pellichero A, Best KL, Routhier F, and Miller WC investigated older adults' experiences and perceptions of a peer-led wheelchair training program. Their findings were published in the Canadian Journal of Occupational Therapy in 2020 (Volume 87, Issue 3, Pages 192-199). 7. Post MWM, Van Asbeck FWA, Van Dijk AJ, and Schrijvers AJP examined the availability of and satisfaction with services for individuals with spinal cord injuries. This study was published in Spinal Cord in 1997 (Volume 35, Issue 2, Pages 109-115). 8. Ragonesi CB and Galloway JC presented a case report on short-term, early intensive power mobility training for an infant at risk for cerebral palsy. The study was published in Pediatric Physical Therapy in 2012 (Volume 24, Issue 2, Pages 141-148). 9. Rice LA, Dysterheft JL, Sanders E, and Rice IM conducted a randomized trial to assess the short-term impact of transfer training among pediatric wheelchair users who use their wheelchairs full-time. The findings were published in the Journal of Spinal Cord Medicine in 2017 (Volume 40, Issue 4, Pages 396-404). 10. Rice LA, Sung JH, Keane K, Peterson E, and Sosnoff JJ conducted a pilot study on a brief fall prevention intervention for manual wheelchair users with spinal cord injuries. The results were published in the Journal of Spinal Cord Medicine in 2020 (Volume 43, Issue 5, Pages 607-615). 11. Rigot SK, DiGiovine KM, Boninger ML, Hibbs R, Smith I, and Worobey LA evaluated the effectiveness of a web-based, direct-to-user transfer training program through a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2021. 12. Routhier F, Kirby RL, Demers L, Depa M, and Thompson K assessed the efficacy and retention of the French-Canadian version of the wheelchair skills training program for manual wheelchair users through a randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2012 (Volume 93, Issue 6, Pages 940-948). 13. Rusek CT, Kleven M, Walker C, Walker K, Heeb R, and Morgan KA conducted a qualitative analysis of inpatient rehabilitation clinicians' perspectives on the state of manual wheelchair training. The study was published in Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology in 2021. 14. Sakakibara BM, Miller WC, Souza M, Nikolova V, and Best KL conducted a pilot study on wheelchair skills training to improve confidence in using manual wheelchairs among older adults. The findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2013 (Volume 94, Issue 6, Pages 1031-1037). 15. Salatino C, Andrich R, Converti RM, and Saruggia M conducted an observational study on powered wheelchair provision in Italy. The study was published in Assistive Technology in 2016 (Volume 28, Issue 1, Pages 41-52). 16. Sarigul-Klijn Y, Lobo-Prat J, Smith BW, Thayer S, Zondervan D, Chan V, et al. explored motor learning in individuals with chronic stroke by acquiring a novel bimanual wheelchair skill using unmasking technology. The findings were presented at the IEEE International Conference on Rehabilitation Robotics in 2017. 17. Wong S investigated the process of learning to use a rear-mounted power assist for manual wheelchairs. The study was published in Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology in 2018 (Volume 13, Issue 8, Pages 772-776). 18. Sawatzky B, Rushton PW, Denison I, and McDonald R conducted a pilot study on a wheelchair skills training program for children. The findings were published in the Australian Occupational Therapy Journal in 2012 (Volume 59, Issue 1, Pages 2-9). 19. Smith EM, Best KL, and Miller WC developed a condensed wheelchair skills training boot camp to improve students' self-efficacy in assessing, training, spotting, and documenting manual and power wheelchair skills. The study was published in Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology in 2020 (Volume 15, Issue 4, Pages 418-420). 20. Smith EM, Sakakibara BM, and Miller WC reviewed factors influencing participation in social and community activities for wheelchair users. The review was published in Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology in 2016 (Volume 11, Issue 5, Pages 361-374). 21. Stanton KM, Pepping M, Brockway JA, Bliss L, Frankel D, and Waggener S utilized an interdisciplinary approach to wheelchair transfer training for individuals with right cerebral dysfunctions. The study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 1983 (Volume 64, Issue 6, Pages 276-280). 22. Štefanac S, Grabovac I, and Fristedt S evaluated wheelchair users' satisfaction with prescribed wheelchairs and wheelchair services in Croatia. The study was published in Collegium Antropologicum in 2018 (Volume 42, Issue 3, Pages 199-210). 23. Suzuki KM and Lockette G conducted a client satisfaction survey of a wheelchair seating clinic. The findings were published in Physical and Occupational Therapy in Geriatrics in 2000 (Volume 17, Issue 2, Pages 55-65). 24. Tasiemski T, Wilski M, and Urbanski P evaluated the effects of a community peer-based wheelchair skills training camp in Morocco as part of the One World Project. The study was published in Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology in 2021. 25. Taylor S, Gassaway J, Heisler-Variale LA, Kozlowski A, Teeter L, LaBarbera J, et al. analyzed patterns in wheeled mobility skills training, equipment evaluation, and utilization as part of the SCI Rehab Project. The findings were published in Assistive Technology in 2015 (Volume 27, Issue 2, Pages 59-68). 26. Toro ML, Eke C, and Pearlman J assessed the impact of the World Health Organization's 8-step wheelchair service provision model on wheelchair users in resource-limited settings through a cohort study in Indonesia. The study was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2016 (Volume 16, Issue 1). 27. Toro-Hernandez ML, Alvarez L, Vargas-Chaparro MC, and Goldberg M evaluated final-year occupational therapy students' knowledge of basic manual wheelchair provision in Colombia. The study was published in Occupational Therapy International in 2020. 28. Trefler E, Fitzgerald SG, Hobson DA, Bursick T, and Joseph R examined the outcomes of wheelchair systems intervention among residents of long-term care facilities. The study was published in Assistive Technology in 2004 (Volume 16, Issue 1, Pages 18-27). 29. Van Der Scheer JW, De Groot S, Tepper M, Faber W, Veeger DH, and Van Der Woude LHV conducted a randomized controlled trial on low-intensity wheelchair training for inactive individuals with long-term spinal cord injuries. The study was published in the Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine in 2016 (Volume 48, Issue 1, Pages 33-42). 30. Verza R, Lopes Carvalho ML, Battaglia MA, and Messmer Uccelli M demonstrated that an interdisciplinary approach to evaluating the need for assistive technology reduces equipment abandonment. The study was published in Multiple Sclerosis in 2006 (Volume 12, Issue 1, Pages 88-93). 31. Visagie S, Mlambo T, van der Veen J, Nhunzvi C, Tigere D, and Scheffler E assessed the impact of structured wheelchair services on user satisfaction and functionality in Zimbabwe. The study was published in the African Journal of Disability in 2016 (Volume 5, Issue 1). 32. Webster JS, McFarland PT, Rapport LJ, Morrill B, Roades LA, and Abadee PS evaluated computer-assisted training to improve wheelchair mobility in patients with unilateral neglect. The study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2001 (Volume 82, Issue 6, Pages 769-775). 33. Williams E, Hurwitz E, Obaga I, Onguti B, Rivera A, Sy TRL, et al. conducted a qualitative study on basic wheelchair users' perspectives on improving access to wheelchair services in Kenya and the Philippines. The study was published in BMC International Health & Human Rights in 2017 (Volume 17, Issue 1). 34. The World Health Organization published guidelines on the provision of manual wheelchairs in resource-limited settings in 2008, based in Geneva, Switzerland. 35. Worobey LA, Kirby RL, Heinemann AW, Krobot EA, Dyson-Hudson TA, Cowan RE, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of group wheelchair skills training for individuals with spinal cord injuries through a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation. 36. Worobey LA, McKernan G, Toro M, Pearlman J, Cowan RE, Heinemann AW, et al. assessed the effectiveness of group wheelchair maintenance training for individuals with spinal cord injuries through a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2021. 37. Worobey LA, Rigot SK, Hogaboom NS, Venus C, and Boninger ML investigated the efficacy of web-based transfer training on independent wheelchair transfers through randomized controlled trials. The study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation.
